title: Two Services, One File
story:
**#kestrel-dev, 02:14**

Amara: the hit counter works on my laptop!!

Amara: it needs redis. `app/app.py` reads `REDIS_HOST` from the environment. I was running redis in a tmux pane. don't ask.

Amara: can you put both in one compose file? project name `weather-desk`. the API is `api` on port 8100, redis is `cache`, and api shouldn't start before cache exists. I'm going to sleep.
objectives: Service `api` runs `python:3.12-alpine` with command `python /app/app.py`, mounts `./app` at `/app` read-only, publishes 8100 to 8000, sets `REDIS_HOST=cache` and declares `depends_on: cache`
Start the project so http://localhost:8100 returns the hit counter
startingState: `/workspace/app/app.py` is Amara's counter service; nothing is running yet.
hints: Both programs go into one `compose.yaml` under `services:`. Services on the same Compose project can reach each other by service name, so the API only needs the right hostname handed to it as an environment variable.

Give `api` an `environment:` block whose value is the name of the redis service, and a `depends_on:` list so Compose starts `cache` first. Because the code lives in `./app`, mount that folder and set `command:` to run the script from the mounted path.

A full file for this mission looks like this. Save it as `compose.yaml` and run `docker compose up -d`:

```yaml
name: weather-desk
services:
  cache:
    image: redis:7-alpine
  api:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    command: python /app/app.py
    volumes:
      - ./app:/app:ro
    ports:
      - "8100:8000"
    environment:
      REDIS_HOST: cache
    depends_on:
      - cache
```

files.content:
import os, socket
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

HOST = os.environ["REDIS_HOST"]


def bump():
    with socket.create_connection((HOST, 6379), timeout=2) as s:
        s.sendall(b"INCR hits\r\n")
        return int(s.recv(64).strip()[1:])


class Desk(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        body = f"WEATHER DESK hits={bump()}\n".encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)


HTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", 8000), Desk).serve_forever()

params.command: docker compose -p weather-desk exec -T api printenv REDIS_HOST

validation.description: http://localhost:8100 returns the hit counter from redis

solution:
cat > compose.yaml <<'EOF'
name: weather-desk
services:
  cache:
    image: redis:7-alpine
  api:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    command: python /app/app.py
    volumes:
      - ./app:/app:ro
    ports:
      - "8100:8000"
    environment:
      REDIS_HOST: cache
    depends_on:
      - cache
EOF
debrief: Compose gives every project its own network where each service name is a DNS name, so `REDIS_HOST: cache` is all the wiring the API needs. Pro tip: `depends_on` only orders container start, not readiness -- if the dependency needs time to become usable, pair it with a healthcheck.
